_comment: Fragment 75 — D-120: the disposable development environment; a withheld credential narrower than it reads; a correction that reached two tiers and missed the third. Merged 2026-08-25.

nodes.label: D-120 — The Development Database Is Disposable and Separate
nodes.description: Development runs against a local stack started from the command line, separate from the deployed branch and from the provisioned project. The database it creates exists to be applied to, tested against, and destroyed.
nodes.rationale: Separating the environment is what makes an irreversible migration testable at all. Applying it to a disposable database costs nothing to get wrong; applying it to the provisioned one is the act nobody has authorized.

nodes.label: A Withheld Credential Narrower Than It Reads
nodes.description: The withheld dependency is the hosted project's credentials pulled into a local environment file, and nothing else. A locally started stack uses none of them, so the database test that appeared blocked was never blocked.
nodes.rationale: A withheld item read broadly stops work it never named. Reading it narrowly separates what genuinely cannot be verified — behaviour against the real project — from what can be verified today and had simply never been attempted.

nodes.label: A Correction That Reached Two Tiers and Missed the One That Is Read
nodes.description: A completion criterion was corrected because it required a live database while the credentials for one were deliberately withheld. The corrected wording landed in the planning journal and the product specification, and not in the build sequence.
nodes.rationale: The missed document is the one a build lane actually reads, so a lane could satisfy the operative text with a test that starts no database and contradict nothing. The propagation sweep verifies that an identifier arrives, never that a phrase removed from one tier is missing from another.

nodes.label: The Tool Is Supplied; the Command Is Not Run
nodes.description: The orchestration lane installs the command-line tool, the script names that wrap it, and the ignore entries for its scratch state. Initialising the project writes a file on the build lane's own surface, so the build lane runs it.
nodes.rationale: Provisioning ahead exists so a mid-sprint request is rare, and it stops precisely at the surface boundary. Tracked migrations and the configuration file are artifacts; only the tool's runtime scratch is ignored.
